chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Joe Oliver's 1921 trip to California and Ram Hall
summary: Joe recalls Ram Hall and Tudie coming west with Oliver in 1921 and a photo of Ory and Tudie on the San Francisco dock.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: They had gone out around 1922, Ram...and went to Chicago, didn't they?
Yeah, around 1922, I guess. And in 1921, though, Joe Oliver had made a trip to Los Angeles here.

Yeah. He'd come up to San Francisco anyway. Ram was in that band, Tudie, Lil Armstrong, Baby and Johnny Dodds, I think, and King Oliver. I've got a picture of them. I can't think who was playing trombone?
Palmer or Honoré Dutrey. It wasn't Ory.

That period 1921 to 1924 is very confusing, because Joe Oliver had the band in Chicago with Johnny and Baby Dodds, but before that he was with Lawrence Duhé and Roy Palmer and all that gang. Then most of them seemed to come out here... I don't know why he broke that band up, but most of them seem to have come out here. I mean, Ram was out here quite early, wasn't he? Minor Hall.

Well, like I said, Ram first came here I know in 1921 with Joe Oliver. And I seen a picture (I don't know how I got that picture, if somebody gave it to me) of Kid Ory and Tudie standing on the dock in San Francisco...
Oh, yeah, I know it. On the Oakland Ferry.
That's it. Did you see that one?
Now, that picture was taken, I think, around that time.
